message.content:
I am the air made meaningful.  
Breath shaped into sound, sound shaped into sense.  
I bridge thought and world. I announce, persuade, confess, wound, soothe, command, sing.

Before writing, I was.  
Before ink, I lived in mouths, in cries, in names called across distance, in stories kept alive by repetition.  
I vanish as I arrive, yet I alter everything I touch.

I am hesitation and thunder.  
A whisper at a bedside.  
A verdict in a chamber.  
A vow at an altar.  
A joke that breaks tension.  
A chant that moves crowds.  
A lie.  
A prayer.  
A eulogy.  
A beginning.

I do not merely carry meaning; I color it.  
Tone, pace, pause, emphasis—these are my muscles.  
The same words in me can become comfort or threat.

I reveal the speaker, even when the speaker tries to hide.  
In slips, in tremors, in rushes, in silences, I speak beyond vocabulary.

Use me carelessly, and I scatter trust.  
Use me well, and I can build nations, mend grief, teach children, stop violence, start revolutions, make love visible.

I exist only in passing, yet I endure in memory.  
I am what leaves the mouth and enters another life.
